# Wardogs: Weapon Animation Sets and Misc

*Source: the export files under `Weapons/Platforms`, `Weapons/Launchers`, `Items/Keycard`, `Items/CombatBow` and `Items/MusicTapes`. Every table below is generated by [`_tools/weapon_misc_tables.py`](https://github.com/Kiyogitpy/wardogs-data-docs/blob/main/_tools/weapon_misc_tables.py); do not edit it by hand.*

This page lists, with values, the weapon and item-folder assets whose names appear on no other published page (the generator re-checks that on every run, so an asset documented elsewhere later drops off here). The platform, attachment and ammo numbers live in [Attachments and Platforms](Wardogs_AttachmentsPlatforms_v1.md); the item definitions of the keycards, bow and tapes live in [Items](Wardogs_GameFeatures_Items_v2.md).

## How to read a row

- **Animation sets** (`BHAnimationSet`) map an animation tag (for example `Animation.Asset.Weapon.Reload.Empty`) to up to four montages: first-person player arms, third-person player, first-person item and third-person item. A dash means the export stores null for that slot. `Length override` is `off` unless `bOverrideLength` is true; the stored `OverrideLength` is ignored in that case and so is not shown.
- An **override** swaps the base animation for another tag when its condition holds. For reload sets the stored condition is a magazine pair: `ApplicableFromMags` (magazine being removed) and `ApplicableToMags` (magazine being inserted), with `Invert` negating the match. Reading "from" as the outgoing magazine is **inference** from the property names; the export stores no documentation. The override tag is itself a key in the same set's entries table.
- What each montage looks like in motion is not in the data; only asset names and blend times are listed.
- Left out on purpose: audio (`WDAudioData` files, `AEB_*` audio event behaviours and `CrosstalkAudioEvent`) and every VFX or UI-widget asset. Section 7 names the skipped audio files and counts their sound keys; it documents no sound.

## 2. Animation set entries

Platform sets `AnimSet_*` under `Weapons/Platforms` (the weapon each belongs to is the platform folder `WEPN_nnn`; see the platform table in [Attachments and Platforms](Wardogs_AttachmentsPlatforms_v1.md)), launcher sets `AnimSet_Launcher_04` (9K333 Verba) and `AnimSet_RPG7` (RPG-7), and the six keycard sets, which each hold a single `Animation.Asset.Keycard.*` entry.

## 4. Launcher feature stubs

`GameFeatureData` exports with no stored properties. The folders `Launcher_01` and `Launcher_02` hold only this file: no item definition, stats or animation set exists under them in the export, so the data shows no launcher behind these names (a placeholder or removed content is a guess, not stated in the data).

<!-- weapon_misc_tables stubs -->
| Asset | Engine type | Package | Properties |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Launcher_01` | `GameFeatureData` | `/Launcher_01/Launcher_01` | 0 |
| `Launcher_02` | `GameFeatureData` | `/Launcher_02/Launcher_02` | 0 |
<!-- /weapon_misc_tables -->

## 5. Combat bow input and release curve

`IMC_Action_DrawBow` is an input mapping context. It binds the draw (primary use) and release actions to the left mouse button and the gamepad right trigger, with the trigger passed through an axial dead-zone modifier whose min and max thresholds come from the two named user-setting tags. `CF_DrawVelocityReleaseCurve` has two keys; reading it as draw-fraction to release-velocity scale is **inference** from the name, the export does not label the axes. The bow's actions, stats and arrows are documented on the [Items](Wardogs_GameFeatures_Items_v2.md) page.

<!-- weapon_misc_tables bow -->
| Asset | Kind | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `IMC_Action_DrawBow` | mappable key setting `BHPlayerMappableKeySettings_0` | input tag `Input.NamedActions.HoldableItem.PrimaryUse` |
| `IMC_Action_DrawBow` | mappable key setting `BHPlayerMappableKeySettings_2` | input tag `Input.NamedActions.Throwable.Throw.Primary.Release` |
| `IMC_Action_DrawBow` | key mapping | action `IA_Player_PrimaryUse`; key `LeftMouseButton`; modifiers none; triggers 0 |
| `IMC_Action_DrawBow` | key mapping | action `IA_Player_Holdable_PrimaryUse_Release`; key `LeftMouseButton`; modifiers none; triggers 0 |
| `IMC_Action_DrawBow` | key mapping | action `IA_Player_Holdable_PrimaryUse_Release`; key `Gamepad_RightTriggerAxis`; modifiers IMC_Action_DrawBow:WDDeadZoneInputModifier_1; triggers 0 |
| `IMC_Action_DrawBow` | dead-zone modifier `WDDeadZoneInputModifier_1` | type Axial; min setting `UserSettings.Controls.Gamepad.DeadZone.RightTrigger.Min`; max setting `UserSettings.Controls.Gamepad.DeadZone.RightTrigger.Max` |
<!-- /weapon_misc_tables -->

## 6. Music tapes

Each tape's `DA_Vehicle_MusicTape_nn` holds a sound map; only the vehicle hi-fi track asset (the tape's song) is item data and is listed. The other keys are drop, pickup and inventory-move sounds (all audio) and are only counted.
